text:
Shopify fell about 15% this morning.

Revenue grew 32% to $3.74 billion. Analysts expected $3.75 billion.

That's a miss of about $10 million on a $3.7 billion quarter.

Subscription revenue and sales volume on the platform also came in a little light.

This is what a high-expectations market looks like: close isn't good enough.

Does a 15% drop on a tiny miss make sense to you?
